- Role-based access to historical cases: ensure that archived or old cases are accessible only to authorized roles (e.g., compliance, legal).

agentforceservice.title: Given a scenario, analyze customer requirements to determine an appropriate solution design considering capabilities, limitations, and design trade-offs for the service rep experience.

objectives.title: Given a scenario, analyze customer requirements to determine an appropriate solution design considering capabilities, limitations, and design trade-offs for the service rep experience.

topics.question: The difference between a Lightning App and a Lightning Console App, and when a consultant should recommend a Service Console App over a standard Lightning App for agent workflows
topics.answer:
Lightning App: standard multi-tab experience; each record opens in a new browser tab. Not optimized for agents who need to work on multiple records simultaneously.

Lightning Console App: multi-tab experience within a single browser tab. Agents can have multiple cases, contacts, and accounts open simultaneously in subtabs without losing context. Includes utility bar for persistent tools (phone, macros, notes).

Recommend Service Console when:

- Agents handle multiple concurrent interactions.

- Phone/chat/messaging channels require persistent utility bar components.

- Case context switching is frequent (agents need to move between records without losing position).

For back-office or field users who work one record at a time, a standard Lightning App is sufficient.

topics.question: How to design a Lightning Service Console layout that optimizes agent efficiency for a high-volume phone support team, including the use of utility bar, macros, and split view
topics.answer:
Key design elements:

- Utility Bar: add softphone (CTI), macros, history, and notes components. These persist across all tabs so agents never lose access to their phone tool.

- Macros: automate multi-step repetitive tasks (e.g., send email, update status, add comment) with a single click. Reduce AHT significantly.

- Split View: allows agents to view a list of cases on the left while working a case on the right. Ideal for agents monitoring a queue simultaneously.

- Page layout: prioritize the most-used fields and related lists at the top. Use Dynamic Forms to show/hide fields based on case type or status.

- Quick Text: pre-written phrases accessible during email/chat to reduce typing time.

topics.question: The trade-offs between a single universal agent console layout versus role-specific page layouts for a multi-tier support organization
topics.answer:
| Approach | Pros | Cons |

|---|---|---|

| Single universal layout | Easier to maintain; agents can be moved between tiers without retraining | Cluttered with irrelevant fields/components for each tier |

| Role-specific layouts | Optimized for each tier's workflow; reduces cognitive load | More maintenance overhead; changes must be replicated across layouts |

Recommendation: use role-specific layouts when tiers have meaningfully different workflows (e.g., Tier 1 handles chat with simple scripts; Tier 3 handles escalations requiring technical detail). Use a universal layout when tiers share 80%+ of the same workflow.

topics.question: How Dynamic Forms and Dynamic Related Lists can be used in the Service Console to reduce page clutter and show context-relevant fields based on case record type or status
topics.answer:
- Dynamic Forms: replace static page layouts with field sections that show/hide based on visibility rules. Example: show "Root Cause" and "Engineering Notes" fields only when Case Status = "Escalated to Engineering."

- Dynamic Related Lists: show/hide related lists based on record criteria. Example: show the "Assets" related list only for product-related case record types.

Benefits: agents see only what is relevant to the current case state, reducing scroll and cognitive load. Requires Lightning pages (not available in Classic).

Dynamic Forms are configured in the Lightning App Builder per record type.

topics.question: When a client requires agents to handle multiple cases simultaneously without losing context, which Service Console features should be recommended and why
topics.answer:
- Multi-tab subtabs: each open record gets its own subtab within the console; agents switch without losing state.

- Split View: agents can monitor a list while actively working a case.

- Utility Bar: persistent tools (macros, history, notes) are available regardless of which tab is active.

- Work item preservation: if an agent navigates away, the Omni-Channel work item remains in their queue; they do not lose the assignment.

- Screen Pop (CTI): when a call comes in, the matching case or contact opens automatically, reducing context-switching time.

topics.question: When a client needs agents to see a 360-degree customer view while working a case, how to configure Related Lists, activity timeline, and external data integration in the console
topics.answer:
- Related Lists: add Contact, Account, open cases, purchase history, entitlements, and assets to the case page layout.

- Activity Timeline: shows all emails, calls, tasks, and events related to the contact/account in chronological order.

- External data: use Salesforce Connect (External Objects) to display real-time data from external ERP or order systems without migrating data into Salesforce.

- Custom Lightning components: embed external system data in a panel within the console (e.g., an order lookup component that queries the ERP via Apex callout).

The goal is for the agent to never need to open a second system while working a case.

topics.question: How to configure case feed and feed filters to surface the most actionable information for agents handling technical support cases
topics.answer:
Case Feed: the Chatter-based feed on a case record showing all activity (emails, comments, log calls, status changes) in a timeline.

Feed Filters: allow agents to filter the feed by type (emails only, comments only, activities only). Configuration:

- Enable Case Feed in Service Cloud Setup.

- Add Feed Filters component to the page layout (in Classic) or use the Activity Timeline in Lightning.

- Customize which feed actions are available (email, log a call, change status, internal note).

Best practice: for technical support, ensure "Internal Notes" and "Email" are the primary feed actions, and that the feed is sorted newest-first so agents see the latest update immediately.

topics.question: How Quick Text, macros, and email templates differ in their use cases for improving agent productivity and response consistency
topics.answer:
| Tool | Description | Best Use Case |

|---|---|---|

| Quick Text | Pre-written text snippets inserted anywhere (email, chat, notes) using a shortcut | Short, reusable phrases during live interactions (greetings, closings, common answers) |

| Macros | Automated multi-step instructions (send email, update field, add comment) run with one click | Repetitive multi-action workflows in the console (e.g., "Close case and send resolution email") |

| Email Templates | Pre-formatted email bodies with merge fields, stored for use in case emails | Structured email communications with consistent formatting and dynamic data |

Key difference: Quick Text inserts text. Macros execute actions. Templates format emails. They can be used together (a macro can apply a template).

topics.question: When agents are working in the field or on mobile devices, what Salesforce Mobile App capabilities and limitations must be considered for Service Cloud use cases
topics.answer:
Capabilities:

- View and update case records.

- Log calls and add case comments.

- Access Knowledge articles.

- Receive push notifications for new case assignments.

- Use offline access for records previously viewed (limited sync).

Limitations:

- Service Console multi-tab experience is NOT available on mobile (mobile uses standard record pages).

- Macros are NOT supported in the mobile app.

- Omni-Channel agent presence and routing are NOT fully supported on mobile.

- CTI / softphone utility bar components do not function on mobile.

- Complex page layouts may not render optimally.

Recommendation: design a simplified mobile page layout for field agents. For full console functionality, agents need a desktop browser.

agentforceservice.title: Given a scenario, analyze customer requirements to determine an appropriate solution design considering capabilities, limitations, and design trade-offs for the customer experience.

objectives.title: Given a scenario, analyze customer requirements to determine an appropriate solution design considering capabilities, limitations, and design trade-offs for the customer experience.

topics.question: How to configure email-to-case and web-to-case to ensure consistent customer experience across inbound contact channels
topics.answer:
Email-to-Case:

- Configure a dedicated support email address that forwards to Salesforce.

- Use On-Demand Email-to-Case (recommended) to keep email processing within Salesforce servers.

- Set up auto-response rules to acknowledge receipt immediately.

- Configure assignment rules to route cases from email to the appropriate queue.

Web-to-Case:

- Generate the HTML form in Setup and embed on the support website.

- Map form fields to case fields (Subject, Description, Priority, Product).

- Configure auto-response rules for immediate acknowledgment.

- Limit field collection to what is necessary to avoid form abandonment.

Consistency: both channels should produce cases with the same required fields populated, route to the same assignment rule logic, and trigger the same auto-response. Use a shared auto-response template.

topics.question: How to design a self-service portal using Experience Cloud that minimizes case creation volume while maintaining CSAT for customers who cannot resolve issues independently
topics.answer: Deflection-first design:

topics.question: **Prominent search bar**: search Knowledge articles before showing the case form.
**Article suggestions**: surface related articles as the customer types their issue.
**Agentforce bot**: intercept the customer before case form access; attempt to resolve via AI.
**Progressive case form**: if the customer still cannot resolve, offer the case form — but pre-populate fields where possible (logged-in user context).
**Community answers**: enable peer-to-peer Q&A so customers help each other.
topics.answer: CSAT maintenance: ensure that if self-service fails, escalation to a case is frictionless. Customers who hit a dead end and cannot create a case quickly will have very low CSAT.

topics.question: When a customer requires seamless escalation from a self-service chatbot to a live agent without repeating context, which Service Cloud features support this and what their limitations are
topics.answer:
Features:

- Agentforce AI Agent: when configured with human handoff, passes the full conversation transcript to the live agent in the Omni-Channel work item.

- Messaging for In-App and Web (MIAW): conversation history is preserved in the messaging session when transferring to a live agent.

- Einstein Bot (legacy): supports agent handoff with transcript transfer; requires Live Agent or MIAW.

Limitations:

- Context transfer is limited to the conversation transcript; the agent still must review it manually.

- If the bot is on a different channel than the live agent queue (e.g., bot on web, agent on phone), context cannot be transferred automatically.

- Authenticated vs. unauthenticated sessions affect how much pre-populated customer data is available to the receiving agent.

topics.question: What configuration is required to send automated case status update notifications to customers, and how to avoid over-notification fatigue
topics.answer:
Configuration:

- Email Alerts via Flow or Process Builder triggered on case Status change.

- Notification templates: use email templates with merge fields (Case Number, Status, Next Steps).

- Customer Portal notifications: Experience Cloud can show in-app notifications for case updates.

Avoiding over-notification fatigue:

- Only send notifications for meaningful status changes (e.g., "In Progress" → "Waiting on Customer," "Resolved"). Do not notify on every internal status transition.

- Consolidate: if multiple updates happen in quick succession, consider a short delay (batch window) before sending.

- Allow customer preferences: let customers opt into/out of specific notification types.

- Avoid notifying on auto-response acknowledgment AND status update within seconds of each other.

topics.question: How to design a post-case survey flow in Service Cloud to automatically collect CSAT scores after case closure
topics.answer: Design steps:

topics.question: Create a **Survey** in Salesforce Surveys with a CSAT question (1–5 scale) and optional open-text follow-up.
Build a **Record-Triggered Flow** on the Case object: trigger = Status changed to "Closed."
Flow action: use "Send Survey Invitation" to send the survey via email to the case contact.
Set a **time delay** (e.g., 1 hour after closure) to avoid sending before the customer has seen the resolution.
Store survey responses linked to the Case record for reporting.
Build a **report** on Survey Response to calculate average CSAT score by agent, queue, or channel.
What configuration triggers the survey send in a post-case CSAT survey flow
topics.answer:
The trigger is a Record-Triggered Flow on the Case object where the entry condition is:

- Object: Case

- Trigger: Record is Updated

- Condition: Status equals "Closed" (AND Status was not previously "Closed" to prevent re-triggering on edits to already-closed cases)

The flow then uses a scheduled path (e.g., 1 hour after the trigger) to send the survey invitation, ensuring the customer has time to experience the resolution before receiving the survey.

topics.question: The design trade-offs between a fully branded Experience Cloud customer portal versus a third-party support website integrated via API for customer-facing support
topics.answer:
| Approach | Pros | Cons |

|---|---|---|

| Experience Cloud portal | Native Salesforce integration; real-time case/Knowledge data; no integration overhead; lower long-term cost | Less design flexibility; Salesforce-hosted; branding limited to Experience Builder themes |

| Third-party website + API | Full design freedom; existing web team can maintain it; can integrate other data sources | Integration complexity; API call limits; data sync latency; ongoing maintenance cost |

Recommend Experience Cloud when: the company wants a fast, Salesforce-native self-service experience with minimal integration work.

Recommend third-party when: the company has an existing web platform with significant investment and complex branding/UX requirements that Experience Builder cannot meet.

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of customer data security and compliance requirements, determine a successful design to secure the data.

objectives.title: Given a set of customer data security and compliance requirements, determine a successful design to secure the data.

topics.question: The difference between object-level, record-level, and field-level security in Salesforce
topics.answer:
- Object-Level Security (OLS): controls whether a user can see the Case object at all (Read, Create, Edit, Delete, View All, Modify All). Set via Profiles and Permission Sets.

- Record-Level Security: controls which specific Case records a user can access. Enforced by OWD, Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules, and Manual Sharing.

- Field-Level Security (FLS): controls whether a user can see or edit a specific field (e.g., SSN, Credit Card) on a record they already have access to. Set via Profiles and Permission Sets.

Think of it as: OLS = can you enter the building? Record-level = which rooms can you enter? FLS = which drawers can you open?

topics.question: When object-level, record-level, and field-level security must be applied together to meet a compliance requirement
topics.answer:
Example: HIPAA compliance for a healthcare contact center.

- OLS: only licensed clinical staff and support agents have Read access to the MedicalCase custom object.

- Record-level: agents can only see cases assigned to their region (OWD = Private + role hierarchy sharing).

- FLS: agents can see the case but cannot see the Diagnosis Code field; only clinical staff have FLS access to that field.

All three layers must be applied together because each layer addresses a different axis of access. Relying on only one layer leaves gaps.

topics.question: How the Case OWD (Organization-Wide Default) setting interacts with role hierarchy, sharing rules, and queue membership to determine which agents can view and edit cases
topics.answer:
OWD sets the baseline: if Case OWD = Private, users can only see cases they own by default.

Role Hierarchy opens access upward: managers in a higher role than the case owner can see records owned by their subordinates.

Sharing Rules extend access horizontally: cases owned by users in Group A can be shared with users in Group B (e.g., cross-regional sharing), without changing OWD.

Queue membership: members of a queue can see all cases assigned to that queue, regardless of OWD. Cases in a queue are owned by the queue, so queue members get access.

The layered model means OWD restricts, and each subsequent mechanism opens access selectively.

topics.question: How to design record-level security for cases so that agents can only see cases assigned to their team, while managers can see all cases in their region
topics.answer:
Design:

- Set Case OWD = Private.

- Create a Role Hierarchy with Region Manager above Team Lead above Agent.

- Assign agents to their team lead's subordinate role; assign team leads to the region manager's subordinate role.

- With O role hierarchy: agents see only their own cases; team leads see all cases owned by their agents; region managers see all cases in their region.

No sharing rules are needed for this basic structure. If agents need to collaborate across teams within a region, add sharing rules or use queues.

topics.question: How to use sharing rules and manual sharing in Service Cloud to extend record visibility to cross-regional teams without opening the OWD
topics.answer:
- Criteria-based sharing rules: share cases matching certain criteria (e.g., Case Region = "West") with a specific group or role. This does not change OWD — it only extends access for cases meeting the criteria.

- Owner-based sharing rules: share all cases owned by users in Role A with users in Role B.

- Manual Sharing: an agent or admin can manually share a specific case with another user or group on an ad-hoc basis. Uses the "Sharing" button on the record.

Both approaches extend visibility without opening OWD to Public Read or Public Read/Write, preserving the security model.

topics.question: When field-level security must restrict agents from seeing customer PII on case records while still allowing access to case details, how to configure this in Salesforce
topics.answer:
- Identify PII fields (e.g., SSN, Date of Birth, Credit Card Number).

- For the agent Profile or Permission Set, set FLS on those fields to Hidden (no Read, no Edit access).

- Agents will see the case record (OLS grants access) but PII fields will be blank and not visible.

- For supervisor/compliance Permission Sets, grant Read (or Read/Edit) FLS on the same fields.

- Use Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption to encrypt PII fields at rest for an additional security layer beyond FLS.

FLS is applied at the profile/permission set level — it does not affect API access unless you also restrict API access separately.

agentforceservice.title: Explain the Knowledge article lifecycle, Knowledge Centered Service (KCS), and Salesforce Knowledge Management configuration.

objectives.title: Explain the Knowledge article lifecycle, Knowledge Centered Service (KCS), and Salesforce Knowledge Management configuration.

topics.question: The stages of the Salesforce Knowledge article lifecycle from draft to published to archived
**Draft**: article is created and being authored. Not visible to agents or customers.
**In Review** (optional, via approval process): article submitted for editorial or compliance review.
**Published**: article is live and visible to permitted audiences (agents, customers, partners based on data category visibility).
**Archived**: article is removed from active search results but retained for historical reference. Linked cases are not affected; the link remains but the article is marked archived.
topics.answer: Articles can be versioned: editing a published article creates a new draft version while the current published version remains live until the new version is published.

topics.question: How Knowledge article versioning works in Salesforce
topics.answer:
When you edit a published article, Salesforce creates a new draft version while keeping the currently published version live. Agents and customers continue to see the current version until the new version is published.

- Each version has its own Version Number.

- Publishing the new version archives the previous version automatically.

- You can view version history on the article record.

- Cases linked to an older version retain the link; the article detail page shows which version was attached.

This prevents disruption to agents working with current information while updates are being reviewed.

topics.question: How Knowledge Centered Service (KCS) methodology aligns with Salesforce Knowledge workflows
topics.answer:
KCS is a methodology where knowledge is created and improved as a natural byproduct of resolving issues — not as a separate documentation project.

Alignment with Salesforce Knowledge:

- Capture: agents create draft articles from within the case (case deflection/knowledge capture components).

- Structure: article record types enforce consistent format (symptoms, environment, resolution).

- Reuse: agents search and attach existing articles to cases before creating new ones.

- Improve: article ratings, feedback, and usage metrics trigger review workflows for stale content.

- Retire: articles that are no longer relevant are archived.

KCS emphasizes that every agent is a knowledge contributor, not just dedicated knowledge managers.

topics.question: What KCS principles should drive article creation governance
topics.answer:
Core KCS principles:

- Capture knowledge at the point of need: create or update articles during case resolution, not after.

- Relevance over perfection: a good-enough article published quickly is more valuable than a perfect article published later.

- Collective ownership: the whole team is responsible for knowledge quality; any agent can flag an article for improvement.

- Demand-driven content: create articles for issues that recur; avoid creating speculative articles.

- Review frequency tied to usage: high-traffic articles get reviewed more often; low-traffic articles are candidates for archiving.

Governance: use workflow/approval processes to enforce review cycles without creating bottlenecks.

topics.question: Which user roles can transition Knowledge articles between lifecycle states
topics.answer:
Transitions depend on Knowledge permission sets and org configuration:

| Permission | Can Do |

|---|---|

| Knowledge Author | Create and edit draft articles; submit for approval |

| Knowledge Publisher | Publish, archive, and restore articles |

| Knowledge Manager | Full control: create, edit, publish, archive, manage data categories and record types |

| Knowledge Viewer | Read-only access to published articles |

Note: "Manage Salesforce Knowledge" system permission is required for full admin control. Publication rights can also be granted via approval process final approval actions.

topics.question: The role of the Knowledge Manager, Author, Publisher, and Viewer permission sets in the article lifecycle and how they enforce governance
topics.answer:
- Knowledge Manager: controls taxonomy (data categories, record types), monitors article quality metrics, manages approval processes. Serves as the governance owner.

- Author: creates articles from case interactions; flags articles for review; cannot publish directly if an approval process is in place.

- Publisher: reviews submitted articles for quality and accuracy; publishes or rejects drafts; ensures compliance before content goes live.

- Viewer: agents or customers who can search and read published articles but cannot create or modify them.

This four-role model enforces a content governance workflow where creation and publication are separated, preventing low-quality articles from going live unchecked.

topics.question: How to configure multiple Knowledge article record types in Salesforce
Enable Salesforce Knowledge in Setup.
Navigate to Setup > Knowledge > Article Types (Classic) or Setup > Object Manager > Knowledge (Lightning) to create record types.
Create a record type for each article category (e.g., "Internal Procedure," "External FAQ," "Product Release Note").
Assign page layouts per record type to control which fields appear for each article type.
Assign record type access to profiles/permission sets as needed.
topics.answer: Each record type can have its own fields, page layout, and approval process, allowing different governance workflows per article category.

topics.question: When using separate record types for internal procedures versus external FAQs is preferable to a single article type
topics.answer:
Use separate record types when:

- Internal procedures have different fields than external FAQs (e.g., internal articles have "Escalation Path" field; external FAQs do not).

- Different approval workflows apply (internal procedures approved by operations manager; external FAQs approved by legal/marketing).

- Different audiences need different layouts (internal-facing vs. customer-facing content looks different).

- You want to restrict data category visibility differently per article type.

Use a single record type when: the content structure is identical and the only difference is audience visibility (controlled via data categories and channel visibility settings instead).

topics.question: How to configure data categories in Salesforce Knowledge
Setup > Data Category Setup > Create a Category Group (e.g., "Products," "Regions").
Add categories within each group (e.g., under "Products": "Hardware," "Software," "Services").
Assign the Category Group to Knowledge (and other objects like Cases, if needed).
On each Knowledge article, set the appropriate data category values.
Configure data category visibility on profiles/permission sets to control which users see which category of articles.
topics.answer: Data categories serve dual purpose: filtering/searching articles and controlling article visibility.

topics.question: Why category hierarchies affect both article visibility and search relevance in Salesforce Knowledge
topics.answer:
Visibility: data category visibility settings cascade down the hierarchy. If a user has access to "Software," they automatically see articles tagged with "Software > CRM" and "Software > ERP" (child categories). Restricting access to "Software" removes access to all child categories as well.

Search relevance: Salesforce Knowledge search uses data categories as a filter. Articles categorized under the user's accessible categories surface in search; articles outside their visibility do not appear, regardless of keyword match.

Implication: designing a shallow category hierarchy makes articles easier to find; overly deep hierarchies fragment articles and reduce search relevance.

topics.question: How to configure article approval processes using Salesforce workflow or approval processes to ensure content quality before publishing
In Setup, go to **Approval Processes** for the Knowledge Article Version object.
Create an approval process with entry criteria (e.g., Status = "In Review" or a custom "Ready for Review" checkbox).
Define approver steps: single approver (Knowledge Publisher), or sequential/parallel approval with multiple reviewers.
Configure final approval action: set Status to "Published" (automatically publishes the article upon final approval).
Configure rejection action: return to draft with a rejection comment notification to the author.
topics.answer: This ensures no article goes live without human review, which is critical for compliance-heavy environments.

topics.question: How article feedback and ratings can be used to identify stale or low-quality knowledge articles and trigger review workflows
topics.answer:
- Salesforce Knowledge supports thumbs up/down ratings and written feedback on articles.

- Track aggregate ratings using Knowledge article reports (KnowledgeArticleViewStat, KnowledgeArticleVoteStat).

- Set a threshold: articles with a vote ratio below (e.g., 60% positive) after a minimum vote count are flagged for review.

- Use Record-Triggered Flows or scheduled reports to create a Task or chatter notification to the Knowledge Manager when an article falls below the quality threshold.

- Article Feedback: agents can submit written feedback directly on an article, which the Knowledge Manager reviews.

topics.question: What happens to linked cases when a Knowledge article is archived or replaced by a new version
topics.answer:
- Archived article: the article link on the case remains intact. The case record shows the article is attached, but the article is in "Archived" status. Agents can still navigate to the archived article and read it; it just no longer appears in active search results.

- New version published: when a new version is published, the previous version is automatically archived. Case links that pointed to the old version now resolve to the archived version. They do not automatically update to the new version.

Takeaway: archiving does not break case-article links. Links are preserved for historical accuracy and compliance purposes.

topics.question: What is required to import existing articles from a legacy knowledge base into Salesforce Knowledge, including the Knowledge Article CSV import process and its limitations
topics.answer:
Requirements:

- Articles must be formatted in CSV files with one file per article record type and separate CSV files for translations (if applicable).

- One ZIP file containing the CSV and any associated file attachments.

- Articles must map to existing Salesforce Knowledge record types and data categories.

Process: Setup > Knowledge > Article Import and Export > Import Articles.

Limitations:

- Maximum of 10,000 articles per import job.

- File size limits per import ZIP.

- Rich text formatting (HTML) can lose formatting during import.

- Does not import article version history from the legacy system — only the current version is imported.

- Data category values in the CSV must exactly match existing Salesforce data category names.

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of requirements, determine how to configure Knowledge to deliver service support and self-service processes.

objectives.title: Given a set of requirements, determine how to configure Knowledge to deliver service support and self-service processes.

topics.question: When agents need to search and attach Knowledge articles to cases from within the Service Console, what configuration is required and which components must be added to the page layout
topics.answer: Configuration:

topics.question: Enable Salesforce Knowledge in Setup.
Enable **Knowledge on Cases** (Setup > Knowledge Settings > Allow users to create and edit articles from the Case Detail page).
Add the **Knowledge component** (Lightning component) to the Case Lightning record page in the App Builder.
Ensure agents have at least the Knowledge Viewer permission set.
topics.answer:
Components:

- Knowledge Component: the main search and attach widget on the case page. Agents type keywords and see suggested articles.

- Suggested Articles: auto-surfaces articles based on case fields (Subject, Description) as soon as the case is saved.

Without the Knowledge component on the page layout, agents must navigate away from the case to find articles.

topics.question: How to use the Knowledge Lightning component versus the Knowledge sidebar to surface relevant articles based on case fields and search terms
topics.answer:
Knowledge Lightning Component (modern, Lightning Experience):

- Embedded on the case record page via App Builder.

- Surfaces suggested articles based on case Subject and Description using search indexing.

- Agents can search, preview, and attach articles without leaving the case.

- Configurable to show specific article types.

Knowledge Sidebar (legacy, Salesforce Classic):

- A sidebar panel in the Classic console that auto-searches based on case Subject.

- Less configurable than the Lightning component.

For Lightning-based implementations, use the Knowledge Lightning Component. The sidebar is a Classic-era feature and should not be the primary recommendation for modern implementations.

topics.question: How data category visibility and role hierarchy interact to determine which users see which published Knowledge articles in an org with multiple customer segments
topics.answer:
- Data category visibility is set per profile or permission set — not per role.

- If a user's profile grants visibility to the "Enterprise" data category, they see all articles tagged "Enterprise" regardless of their position in the role hierarchy.

- Role hierarchy does NOT cascade data category visibility (unlike record sharing). A manager does not automatically see categories their subordinates can see unless the manager's profile/permission set explicitly grants that visibility.

- In an org with multiple segments (e.g., SMB, Enterprise, Partner), create separate data categories and assign visibility per profile/permission set to match each agent group's customer segment.

topics.question: How to expose Knowledge articles to external customers through an Experience Cloud portal while restricting internal-only articles from being visible
topics.answer:
- Use Channel visibility settings on each article: mark internal articles as visible to "Internal App" only; mark external FAQs as visible to "Public" or "Customer" channels.

- In the Experience Cloud site, the Knowledge component surfaces only articles marked for the "Customer" or "Public" channel.

- Additionally, use data categories: assign internal articles to a data category that has no visibility grant for the Experience Cloud guest user or authenticated customer profile.

Both channel visibility and data category visibility should be used together for defense-in-depth control over article exposure.

topics.question: The design trade-offs between a single article type versus multiple article types in a Knowledge implementation for a company with both internal procedures and external FAQs
topics.answer:
See also: Section on record types. The key trade-offs:

| | Single Article Type | Multiple Article Types |

|---|---|---|

| Maintenance | Simpler; one page layout, one approval process | More complex; separate layouts and processes per type |

| Governance | Harder to enforce different standards per audience | Easier to apply type-specific approval workflows |

| Agent UX | Agents may see irrelevant fields | Fields are tailored to content purpose |

| Reporting | Harder to segment article performance by type | Easy to filter reports by record type |

Recommendation: use multiple record types when content structure, governance, or audience differs meaningfully. Use a single type only for simple, homogeneous knowledge bases.

topics.question: When a company wants to use AI-suggested Knowledge articles to assist agents in real time during a chat interaction, what must be configured in Service Cloud
topics.answer:
- Enable Einstein for Service (requires appropriate Service Cloud Einstein license).

- Enable Einstein Article Recommendations in Setup > Einstein > Article Recommendations.

- Train the model: requires a history of cases where articles were attached (minimum data volume required — typically 1,000+ resolved cases with article attachments).

- Add the Einstein Recommendations component to the messaging/chat console page layout.

- During a live chat, Einstein analyzes the conversation and surfaces recommended articles in real time, which agents can share with the customer with one click.

Without sufficient case+article attachment history, the AI model cannot make quality recommendations.

topics.question: How to track Knowledge article usage metrics — views, attachments to cases, and thumbs up/down ratings — and use them to demonstrate ROI of the Knowledge investment
topics.answer:
Metrics to track:

- Views: reported via KnowledgeArticleViewStat (report type: Knowledge Articles).

- Case attachments: cases with a related Knowledge article (use Articles & Cases report type or custom report).

- Thumbs up/down: KnowledgeArticleVoteStat object.

- Deflection: cases NOT created after a knowledge article view in the Experience Cloud portal (measured via Analytics or custom tracking).

ROI calculation:

- AHT reduction: before vs. after knowledge deployment.

- Deflection count x average cost-per-contact = cost savings.

- FCR improvement x volume = repeat contact cost avoidance.

Build a Salesforce Dashboard with components for each metric and present to leadership quarterly.

agentforceservice.title: Given business process requirements, recommend the appropriate approach to intake channels and their design.

objectives.title: Given business process requirements, recommend the appropriate approach to intake channels and their design.

topics.question: How to choose between Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, and the Salesforce-native case submission form based on volume, routing complexity, and automation requirements
topics.answer:
| Channel | Best When |

|---|---|

| Email-to-Case | Customers primarily use email; high volume of inbound email; need email threading (replies append to existing case) |

| Web-to-Case | Customers submit issues via a web form; need structured data capture (dropdowns, required fields); max 5,000 cases/day |

| Native Case Submission (Experience Cloud) | Authenticated customer portal users; need real-time data (existing cases, entitlements visible); richer form logic via Flows |

Routing complexity: all three support assignment rules. Automation: all three support auto-response rules. The key differentiator is channel (email vs. web) and whether customers are authenticated.

topics.question: The difference between On-Demand Email-to-Case and standard Email-to-Case, and when each should be used based on email volume and firewall constraints
topics.answer:
Standard Email-to-Case: requires opening an inbound port on the company's email server to allow Salesforce to receive emails directly. Requires firewall configuration. Appropriate when the company controls email infrastructure and can open ports.

On-Demand Email-to-Case: emails are forwarded to a Salesforce-hosted email service (no firewall port changes required). Salesforce processes the email and creates the case. Preferred approach for most implementations because it does not require firewall changes and is more secure.

Key limit: On-Demand Email-to-Case has a daily email processing limit (standard is 2,500/day; can be increased). Standard Email-to-Case does not have this limit but requires infrastructure access.

topics.question: The design considerations when building a Web-to-Case form, including field mapping, auto-response rules, and case assignment rules
topics.answer:
- Field mapping: only capture fields that are necessary for routing and resolution. Every additional field increases form abandonment.

- Required fields: Subject and Description are essential. Priority, Product, and Case Type improve routing accuracy.

- Auto-response rules: configure a rule that sends an email acknowledgment to the customer immediately upon case creation. Include case number and expected response time in the email.

- Assignment rules: create criteria-based rules that route the case to the correct queue (e.g., Product = "Hardware" → Hardware Support Queue).

- Hidden fields: pass additional metadata (e.g., page URL the customer submitted from) as hidden fields to aid routing without cluttering the form.

- CAPTCHA / spam prevention: add reCAPTCHA to prevent automated spam submissions.

topics.question: How to prevent spam when configuring a Web-to-Case form
topics.answer:
- Add reCAPTCHA: Salesforce Web-to-Case supports Google reCAPTCHA integration. Humans pass; bots fail.

- Required field validation: make Subject and Description required, with minimum character counts, to deter automated submissions.

- Assignment rule filtering: create an assignment rule that routes cases with known spam patterns (certain keywords, invalid email formats) to a Spam queue for human review.

- Flow-based validation: use a Screen Flow for case submission instead of the raw Web-to-Case form; Flows support complex validation logic.

- IP rate limiting: implement at the web layer (not Salesforce) to limit submissions from a single IP.

topics.question: When a company receives support requests through multiple channels (email, phone, chat, social), how to design an Omni-Channel routing strategy that routes to the right queue with the right priority
topics.answer: Design steps:

topics.question: **Define Service Channels**: create one Service Channel per work item type (Case, Chat, Messaging Session, Social Post).
**Create Queues**: one queue per team/skill group (Tier 1 Technical, Billing, Enterprise Support, etc.).
**Configure Routing Configurations**: set capacity and priority per channel per queue. Example: Chat has priority 10 (highest) because it is synchronous; Email has priority 1.
**Assign agents to queues**: agents in a queue receive work from that queue when available.
**Set Presence Configurations**: define which channels an agent can handle and their capacity (e.g., 1 chat + 3 email simultaneously).
**Peak volume**: use queue overflow rules or chatbots to handle volume when agent capacity is exceeded.
How to configure routing rules in Omni-Channel to handle peak volume spikes without overwhelming agents in a specific queue
topics.answer:
- Capacity limits: set agent capacity per channel to prevent overload (e.g., max 2 concurrent chats per agent).

- Queue-based overflow: if a queue's wait time exceeds a threshold, route new items to a secondary queue or trigger a bot interaction.

- Skill-based overflow: expand the eligible agent pool during peak hours by temporarily including agents with adjacent skills.

- Chatbot escalation buffer: deploy a bot to handle tier-1 interactions during peak volume; only escalate to agents when the bot cannot resolve.

- Workforce management: schedule additional agents during predictable peak hours rather than relying solely on routing configuration to manage load.

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of business goals, discuss the use cases and functionality for proposed interaction channels.

objectives.title: Given a set of business goals, discuss the use cases and functionality for proposed interaction channels.

topics.question: How voice integration via Service Cloud Voice works and what telephony options are available (Amazon Connect, partner telephony, Bring Your Own Telephony)
topics.answer:
Service Cloud Voice (SCV) embeds telephony directly into the Service Console so agents handle calls within Salesforce without switching to a separate phone application. It provides real-time call controls, transcription, and screen pop.

Telephony options:

- Amazon Connect (Salesforce-provided): fully managed telephony through Salesforce. No separate telephony contract; Salesforce provisions and manages the Amazon Connect instance. Easiest to set up.

- Partner Telephony: a Salesforce-certified telephony partner's cloud platform is connected to SCV. More flexibility in provider choice; requires partner setup.

- Bring Your Own Telephony (BYOT): the company's existing telephony system is connected via API/CTI. Maximum flexibility; requires the most integration work.

topics.question: When Amazon Connect, partner telephony, or Bring Your Own Telephony is the appropriate choice for Service Cloud Voice
topics.answer:
| Choice | Best When |

|---|---|

| Amazon Connect | Starting fresh; no existing telephony investment; want Salesforce to manage the stack; fastest time to value |

| Partner Telephony | Prefer a specific certified partner (e.g., Genesys, Avaya via SCV); need advanced features the partner provides |

| BYOT | Significant existing telephony investment (on-premise PBX or cloud telephony); cannot or will not replace current phone system |

Cost and complexity: Amazon Connect < Partner Telephony < BYOT (in terms of integration effort).

topics.question: When a company wants to offer both synchronous (chat) and asynchronous (messaging) support, what Service Cloud channels support each and what distinguishes them operationally
topics.answer:
Synchronous channels in Service Cloud:

- Live Agent / Embedded Chat: real-time chat; session ends when either party disconnects.

- Service Cloud Voice: real-time phone calls.

Asynchronous channels:

- Messaging for In-App and Web (MIAW): persistent messaging; customer can leave and return; conversation history preserved.

- SMS/WhatsApp (via Messaging channels): mobile-first async messaging.

Operational distinction: synchronous requires dedicated agent availability; agents handle one interaction at a time (or a small number concurrently). Asynchronous allows agents to manage more conversations because responses are not expected immediately.

topics.question: The use cases for Salesforce Messaging for In-App and Web (MIAW) versus classic Live Agent chat, including handoff to agent and session persistence
topics.answer:
| | MIAW | Classic Live Agent |

|---|---|---|

| Session persistence | Yes — conversation continues even if the customer closes the window | No — session ends when either party disconnects |

| Channel support | In-app, web, SMS, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger | Web only |

| Async support | Yes | No (synchronous only) |

| Agent handoff | Full transcript passed to agent | Transcript passed, but session must be active |

| Bot integration | Agentforce / Einstein Bots integrate natively | Einstein Bots supported but older architecture |

| Salesforce direction | Current investment; preferred | Legacy; being phased toward MIAW |

Recommendation: for new implementations, use MIAW. Classic Live Agent is maintained but Salesforce's strategic direction is MIAW.

topics.question: How Messaging channels (SMS/text, WhatsApp) are enabled in Service Cloud and what configuration steps differentiate messaging setup from chat channel setup
topics.answer: SMS/WhatsApp setup:

topics.question: In Setup, go to **Messaging** (under Messaging Settings).
Create a Messaging Channel (select SMS or WhatsApp).
For WhatsApp: connect a Facebook Business Manager account and a WhatsApp Business Account.
For SMS: provision a phone number via a supported provider (Salesforce-provided or Twilio).
Create a **Service Channel** for Messaging in Omni-Channel.
Create a **Routing Configuration** and assign to a Queue.
Enable agents to handle messaging work items via **Presence Configuration**.
topics.answer: Key difference from chat: chat uses an Embedded Service Deployment (a JavaScript snippet on a website). Messaging uses a phone number or social account as the entry point, not a website embed.

topics.question: The use cases for social media as a service channel, including how Social Customer Service connects social mentions to case creation and agent workflows
topics.answer:
Use cases:

- Monitor Twitter/X, Facebook for brand mentions and customer complaints.

- Create cases automatically from social posts that match keywords (e.g., your brand name + negative sentiment).

- Allow agents to respond to social posts from within the Service Console.

How Social Customer Service works:

topics.question: Connect social accounts (Facebook Page, Twitter/X account) in Setup > Social Customer Service.
Configure keyword matching rules to determine which posts create cases.
Cases are created with the social post content in the Description; the customer's social profile is linked as a Contact.
Agents respond to the case using the Feed Action, which posts the reply back to the original social thread.
topics.answer: Limitation: social channel volume can be high; filtering and keyword rules are critical to avoid creating noise cases.

topics.question: When a company wants to reduce inbound case volume by enabling community-based peer support, how Experience Cloud communities can serve as a deflection channel
topics.answer:
- Deploy an Experience Cloud community with a Q&A or discussion forum component (Chatter Questions).

- Customers post questions; other community members (including expert customers and employees) answer.

- Answered questions become searchable content that deflects future contacts.

- Questions that community members cannot answer are escalated to a case with the conversation history intact.

- Salesforce Knowledge articles can be surfaced alongside community answers to amplify deflection.

Measurement: track the ratio of questions answered by the community vs. escalated to cases to calculate community deflection rate.

topics.question: The difference between an Einstein Bot / Flow Bot and an Agentforce AI Agent in terms of configuration approach, conversation model, and suitable use cases
topics.answer:
| | Einstein Bot / Flow Bot | Agentforce AI Agent |

|---|---|---|

| Configuration | Dialog-tree or Flow-based; explicitly authored conversation paths | Topic + action-based; AI reasons over topics and decides which action to take |

| Conversation model | Scripted; follows defined paths; limited by authored dialogs | Generative; understands natural language; can handle variations without explicit scripting |

| Flexibility | Low — every variation must be scripted | High — handles novel phrasings within topic scope |

| Suitable use cases | Structured, predictable interactions (hours inquiry, reset password via exact steps) | Complex, variable interactions (troubleshooting, multi-step processes, personalized responses) |

| Guardrails | Defined by dialog design | Defined by topic scope, action permissions, and grounding configuration |

Agentforce is Salesforce's strategic direction. Einstein Bots remain valid for simple, structured use cases.

agentforceservice.title: Assess the design considerations and best practices when configuring an interaction channel solution.

objectives.title: Assess the design considerations and best practices when configuring an interaction channel solution.

topics.question: How Service Channels and Routing Configurations must be set up for each work type (case, chat, messaging) before Omni-Channel can route that work item type
topics.answer: Required setup per work type:

topics.question: **Service Channel**: defines the Salesforce object that generates work items (e.g., Case, ChatTranscript, MessagingSession). One Service Channel per work type.
**Routing Configuration**: defines the priority, capacity, and routing model (Queue-Based or Skills-Based) for that channel. Each queue is assigned a Routing Configuration.
**Queue**: agents are members of queues. The queue is linked to the Routing Configuration.
**Presence Configuration**: defines which Service Channels an agent can be present on simultaneously and their capacity limits.
**Agent Presence**: agents must set themselves as "Available" for the appropriate channel in the Omni-Channel widget.
topics.answer: If any step is missing (e.g., no Service Channel for MessagingSession), Omni-Channel cannot route messaging work items.

topics.question: The configuration implications of enabling Enhanced Omni-Channel versus Classic Omni-Channel, and what migration considerations apply
topics.answer:
Classic Omni-Channel: original routing engine; supports basic queue-based routing with capacity models.

Enhanced Omni-Channel: next-generation routing engine with:

- More granular capacity management.

- Support for secondary routing criteria.

- Better Skills-Based Routing integration.

- Required for some newer features (e.g., Unified Routing with Agentforce).

Migration considerations:

- Enabling Enhanced Omni-Channel is a one-way change in some orgs — cannot easily revert.

- Existing routing configurations and queues must be validated post-migration.

- Test all routing scenarios in a sandbox before enabling in production.

- Enhanced routing uses a different capacity model; agent capacity limits may need reconfiguration.

topics.question: What best practices should be followed when configuring Omni-Channel capacity models to balance agent workload and customer wait times
topics.answer:
- Set realistic capacity per channel: do not assign more concurrent work items than an agent can handle with quality (e.g., max 2 concurrent chats for most agents).

- Weight channels differently: synchronous work (chat) counts more toward capacity than async (email). Use relative weights.

- Monitor utilization: use Omni Supervisor to watch real-time agent utilization; adjust capacity if agents are consistently over or under-loaded.

- Test with realistic volume: load test routing in a sandbox before go-live to validate capacity settings at scale.

- Include transfer/wrap-up time: account for after-chat work time in capacity models so agents are not immediately routed new items while completing wrap-up.

topics.question: The design considerations for routing work items using Omni-Channel Skills-Based Routing versus Queue-Based Routing and when skills-based is preferred
topics.answer:
| | Queue-Based Routing | Skills-Based Routing |

|---|---|---|

| How it works | Routes work items to a queue; any available queue member can receive the item | Routes to an agent whose profile matches the required skills |

| Configuration | Simpler; Queues + Routing Config | More complex; define Skills, assign agents skills with proficiency levels |

| Best for | Generalist agent teams; simple routing by product or region | Specialized agents; multi-language support; technical certifications |

| When skills-based is preferred | When matching the customer's language, issue type, or product expertise to an agent is more important than simply distributing load |

Skills-based adds setup complexity but significantly improves FCR and CSAT when agent specialization matters.

topics.question: What the Omni-Channel Supervisor panel provides and how supervisors use it to monitor real-time agent status, queue backlog, and work item wait times
topics.answer:
The Omni-Channel Supervisor (accessible via the Service Console utility bar or as a standalone app) provides:

- Agent Status: real-time view of each agent's presence status (Available, Busy, Offline, custom statuses).

- Agent Work Items: what each agent is currently handling.

- Queue Backlog: how many work items are waiting in each queue.

- Work Item Wait Times: how long each queued item has been waiting.

- Channel breakdown: view metrics by channel (cases vs. chat vs. messaging).

Supervisors use it to: reassign items from overloaded queues, flag agents who have been idle too long, and adjust staffing in real time during peak volume events.

topics.question: How to design auto-response rules for Email-to-Case to acknowledge receipt without creating agent confusion from customer replies to auto-responses
topics.answer:
- Use a no-reply email address as the sender of auto-response emails (e.g., noreply@support.company.com). This prevents customer replies from creating additional emails on the case.

- Do not use the agent's email or the support queue email as the From address of the auto-response.

- Include the case number and a link to the portal in the auto-response so customers can check status without replying.

- Set a clear message: "Thank you for contacting us. Your case #XXXXX has been created. An agent will respond within [timeframe]. Please do not reply to this email."

- Test threading: confirm that auto-responses are not creating new cases due to email threading issues (the In-Reply-To header must match for threading to work).

topics.question: How to configure Embedded Service Deployments for chat, including pre-chat forms, offline support, and branding, and how this differs from a Chat Button configuration
topics.answer: Embedded Service Deployment (modern):

topics.question: Setup > Embedded Service Deployments > New Deployment (Chat type).
Configure: branding (colors, logo, name), availability (online/offline hours).
Add **Pre-Chat form**: fields the customer fills before connecting to an agent (Name, Email, Issue Type). These map to case fields and aid routing.
Set **Offline support**: when no agents are available, redirect to case form or display a message.
Generate a JavaScript snippet and embed on the company's website.
topics.answer:
Chat Button (Classic): a simpler configuration that creates a button on a Visualforce page or website; less feature-rich; does not support pre-chat forms or branding as easily.

For new implementations, use Embedded Service Deployments. Chat Buttons are the legacy approach.

topics.question: How pre-chat data can be used to pre-populate case fields and speed routing in Messaging for In-App and Web
topics.answer:
- During the pre-chat phase of a MIAW interaction, customers submit a form (e.g., Name, Email, Issue Type).

- In Setup > Messaging Channels > Pre-Chat configuration, map pre-chat form fields to standard case fields (Subject, Case Type, Priority).

- When the messaging session is created, these fields are auto-populated on the case, saving agent time.

- Routing use: map Issue Type to a case field, then create an Omni-Channel routing rule based on that field value to route the session to the appropriate queue automatically.

- For authenticated customers, pre-populate pre-chat fields using their profile data so they do not need to re-enter information they have already provided.

topics.question: How pre-chat and post-chat survey configuration works in Messaging for In-App and Web
topics.answer:
Pre-chat: configured as a form within the MIAW channel settings. Fields are presented to the customer before the agent connection is made. Data captured maps to case/messaging session fields.

Post-chat (post-conversation) survey:

topics.question: Create a **Salesforce Survey** with CSAT or NPS questions.
In the MIAW channel configuration, enable the post-conversation survey and link the Survey.
After the messaging session ends (agent marks it complete), the survey is automatically sent to the customer.
Responses are stored in the Survey Response object, linked to the messaging session and contact.
topics.answer: The key configuration point: the survey is triggered by session closure, not by a separate flow, when configured natively within the MIAW channel settings.

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of business requirements, recommend an appropriate use for AI agents in the customer service process.

objectives.title: Given a set of business requirements, recommend an appropriate use for AI agents in the customer service process.

topics.question: What requirements must be met before AI agents can reliably resolve a class of customer service requests, including data quality, knowledge coverage, and action permissions
topics.answer:
Prerequisites:

- Data quality: customer and account data must be accurate and complete so the AI agent can identify the customer and retrieve correct information.

- Knowledge coverage: the Knowledge base must cover the issue types the AI will handle. Gaps in articles lead to incorrect or hallucinated responses.

- Action permissions: the AI agent must have permission to execute the actions required (e.g., look up order status via API, create cases, update records). Permissions must be scoped appropriately.

- Well-defined scope: the AI agent should handle a specific, well-bounded set of request types. Overly broad scope increases the risk of errors.

- Escalation path: a clear, tested handoff to a human agent must exist for cases the AI cannot resolve.

- Sufficient volume: there must be enough volume for the issue type to justify AI automation; otherwise, cost savings do not materialize.

topics.question: When a company wants to automate tier-1 case resolution for password resets and order status inquiries, when is an Agentforce AI agent the right recommendation versus a traditional bot
topics.answer:
Agentforce AI agent is right when:

- The request type has natural language variation (customers phrase the same request many different ways).

- Resolution requires reasoning across multiple steps or data sources (e.g., look up order, check status, determine eligibility for resolution action).

- The company wants the AI to improve over time with usage.

Traditional bot is right when:

- The interaction is highly structured and predictable (exact step-by-step process with no variation).

- A decision tree accurately represents all possible paths.

- The company lacks the Knowledge base or data quality required for generative AI grounding.

For password resets (simple, predictable) a Flow Bot may be sufficient. For order status (variable customer queries, multiple resolution paths) Agentforce AI is the better fit.

topics.question: How to determine the appropriate handoff point from an AI agent to a human agent, and what data should be passed at escalation to preserve customer context
topics.answer:
Handoff triggers:

- AI agent cannot match the customer's request to a known topic after a defined number of attempts.

- Customer explicitly requests a human agent.

- The issue type is flagged as requiring human judgment (e.g., complaints, legal matters, complex billing disputes).

- Sentiment detection identifies an angry or distressed customer.

- The AI agent reaches a configured confidence threshold and determines it cannot resolve with sufficient confidence.

Data passed at escalation:

- Full conversation transcript.

- Customer identity (name, account, contact record).

- Issue summary (what the AI understood the customer's need to be).

- Actions already taken by the AI (e.g., "I looked up order #12345 and it shows shipped").

- Case record if one was created.

The receiving agent should be able to pick up without asking the customer to repeat themselves.

agentforceservice.title: Explain agentic service capabilities, use cases, and configuration processes.

objectives.title: Explain agentic service capabilities, use cases, and configuration processes.

topics.question: What types of actions an Agentforce Service Agent can perform out of the box (e.g., case creation, knowledge retrieval, order lookups) and what requires custom configuration
topics.answer:
Out-of-the-box actions (standard):

- Create a case.

- Search and retrieve Knowledge articles.

- Look up contact/account information.

- Check case status.

- Transfer/escalate to a human agent.

- Send a messaging session summary.

Requires custom configuration:

- Order status lookups from external ERP (requires Apex action or external API connection).

- Custom eligibility checks (requires Flow or Apex action).

- Processing refunds or cancellations (requires custom action with appropriate guardrails).

- Integrations with non-Salesforce systems (requires custom action definitions).

Custom actions are defined as Agent Actions in the Agentforce Agent Builder and are invoked by the AI when the customer's intent matches.

topics.question: How Agentforce for Service is configured, including topics, actions, and the agent builder interface in Salesforce
topics.answer: Configuration steps:

topics.question: **Agent Builder** (Setup > Agentforce > Agents): the central interface for creating and configuring Agentforce agents.
**Create Agent**: name the agent, select type (Service Agent), configure the base persona and instructions.

**Define Topics**: topics define the areas the agent handles (e.g., "Billing Inquiries," "Order Status," "Password Reset"). Each topic has a description that helps the AI determine which topic applies to a customer's message.
**Configure Actions per Topic**: assign standard or custom actions to each topic. Actions are what the AI executes (create case, look up order, retrieve article).
**Guardrails**: define what the agent is NOT allowed to do (e.g., "Do not provide medical advice," "Always escalate complaints about legal matters").
**Test**: use the Agent Builder preview to simulate conversations and validate topic and action routing.
**Publish**: deploy to a channel (MIAW, Experience Cloud).
How to configure and publish an Agentforce Service Agent to a Messaging for In-App and Web channel, including channel linking and testing
topics.answer: Steps:

topics.question: Complete Agent Builder configuration (topics, actions, guardrails).
In the Agent Builder, navigate to **Channels** and select the MIAW messaging channel to link the agent to.
In **Messaging Settings** (Setup > Messaging > Messaging Settings), find the target MIAW channel and confirm the Agentforce agent is assigned.
**Test mode**: use the Agent Builder's built-in preview to simulate conversations. Also test via a sandbox Embedded Service Deployment on a test page.
Validate: confirm escalation to human agent works; confirm topic routing is correct for sample utterances; confirm actions execute correctly.
**Activate** the agent in Agent Builder and confirm the MIAW channel is live.
Monitor using Omni Supervisor and Agentforce Analytics in the initial days after launch.
The limitations of Agentforce Service Agents in terms of supported channels, action complexity, and compliance use cases that require human oversight
topics.answer:
Channel limitations:

- Agentforce Service Agents work primarily on text-based channels (MIAW, web chat, SMS). Voice channel support is limited/evolving.

- Not all Experience Cloud templates support embedded Agentforce agents.

Action complexity limitations:

- Actions must be pre-defined; the AI cannot spontaneously execute actions not in its configured set.

- Long multi-step processes with many conditional branches may be better served by Flows than AI agent actions.

- External API latency affects AI agent response time.

Compliance use cases requiring human oversight:

- Regulated industries (healthcare, finance, legal) may prohibit AI from making commitments or providing advice without human review.

- PII handling by AI agents must comply with data residency and processing regulations.

- Audit trail requirements: all AI actions must be logged; Salesforce logs agent actions, but organizations must verify logging meets compliance standards.

- AI agents should never be the final decision-maker in high-stakes scenarios (e.g., loan approvals, medical recommendations).

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of requirements or KPIs, design a case management solution from creation to closure.

objectives.title: Given a set of requirements or KPIs, design a case management solution from creation to closure.

topics.question: The role of case statuses in lifecycle management and how to design a status picklist that supports KPI reporting without creating agent confusion
topics.answer:
Case statuses define where a case is in its lifecycle and are critical for measuring resolution time, SLA compliance, and agent productivity.

Design principles:

- Each status should have a clear, unambiguous meaning that agents understand.

- Status values should map to KPIs: "Waiting on Customer" pauses SLA clock; "In Progress" keeps it running.

- Avoid too many statuses — 5–8 well-defined values is typically sufficient. More causes agent confusion and inconsistent usage.

- Reserve "Closed" as a terminal status that triggers automation (surveys, case close template).

Example well-designed status set:

New → In Progress → Waiting on Customer → Waiting on Engineering → Resolved → Closed

Include "Closed" as distinct from "Resolved" if post-resolution verification is part of the SLA.

topics.question: How to design assignment rules that route cases to the correct queue based on case origin, product, priority, and customer tier
topics.answer: Assignment Rules evaluate criteria top-to-bottom and apply the first matching rule:

topics.question: Setup > Case Assignment Rules > New Rule.
Add Rule Entries with criteria and an assigned queue or user.
topics.answer: Example rule entries (in priority order):

topics.question: Case Origin = "Phone" AND Priority = "Critical" → P1 Critical Support Queue.
Product = "Hardware" → Hardware Support Queue.
Account: Customer Tier = "Enterprise" → Enterprise Support Queue.
Default (catch-all) → General Support Queue.
topics.answer:
Best practices:

- Order rules from most specific to least specific.

- Every case should match at least the catch-all rule.

- Test rules in a sandbox with cases that represent all expected variations.

- Use formula criteria for complex conditions that basic field picklists cannot handle.

topics.question: How to use case queues, assignment rules, and Omni-Channel together to create an end-to-end routing architecture for a multi-tier support model
topics.answer: End-to-end architecture:

topics.question: **Case creation** (Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case, manual): case is created.
**Assignment Rule** fires immediately: evaluates criteria (product, priority, origin) and assigns the case to the appropriate **Queue**.
**Omni-Channel** detects a new case in the queue: the work item is pushed to an available, appropriately configured agent who is a member of that queue.
**Agent accepts** the work item via the Omni-Channel widget: the case is assigned to the agent; they begin working.
**Escalation rules**: if the case is not updated within a defined period, it is escalated to a higher-tier queue and Omni-Channel re-routes.
topics.answer: Queues serve as the staging area between assignment rules and Omni-Channel routing. This architecture cleanly separates routing logic (assignment rules) from agent distribution (Omni-Channel).

topics.question: How email threading in Email-to-Case works so that customer replies are appended to the existing case rather than creating duplicate cases, and what can break this behavior
topics.answer:
Threading mechanism: when Salesforce sends an email from a case, it includes a unique thread ID in the email body (typically in the footer or headers). When the customer replies, the reply contains that thread ID, which Salesforce uses to match the email to the existing case.

What breaks threading:

- Customer modifies the email subject line (removes the case number from the subject).

- Customer emails a new address instead of replying (no thread ID in the new email).

- Customer uses a different email client that strips footer content.

- The thread ID is deleted from the email body by the customer.

- Email is forwarded rather than replied to.

Best practice: include the thread ID in multiple locations (subject line with case number AND footer) to maximize threading reliability.

topics.question: The use cases for case escalation rules versus workflow-based escalation, including which is more appropriate when time-sensitive SLA thresholds must be enforced
topics.answer:
| | Case Escalation Rules | Workflow/Flow-based Escalation |

|---|---|---|

| Best for | Time-based SLA escalation (case not updated in X hours) | Field-change-based escalation (Priority changed to Critical → notify manager) |

| Trigger | Time elapsed since case creation or last modification | Record save or field change |

| Actions | Reassign case, send email alert | More flexible: field update, email, Chatter post, external callout |

| SLA enforcement | Best fit — designed for time-based thresholds | Not ideal for time-based rules (requires scheduled flows) |

Recommendation: use Case Escalation Rules for time-sensitive SLA thresholds (e.g., "Escalate if Priority = High and no update in 2 hours"). Use Flow-based automation for event-driven escalation (e.g., "When customer replies and case status is Closed, re-open case and notify supervisor").

topics.question: How to configure case teams to support multi-agent collaboration on a single case, and what limitations exist with case team roles
topics.answer: Case Teams allow multiple agents (with different roles) to collaborate on a single case:

topics.question: Setup > Case Team Roles: define roles (e.g., "Tier 2 Specialist," "Account Manager," "Quality Reviewer") with read or read/write access.
Add team members to a case via the Case Team related list.
Use **Predefined Case Teams** (templates) for common team configurations to speed up team setup.
topics.answer:
Access: each team member's role controls their case access level (read vs. read/write).

Limitations:

- Case team roles do not replace case ownership — there is still one case owner.

- Maximum of 5 predefined case teams per org (standard configuration; can be increased).

- Case team members are not automatically notified of case updates unless notification rules are configured.

- Team members cannot be automatically added by automation rules — an agent or admin must add them manually or via Apex/Flow.

topics.question: How parent-child case relationships work in Salesforce and when splitting a complex issue into child cases is preferable to managing it as a single record
topics.answer:
Parent-Child Cases: a parent case (container/master) can have multiple child cases linked to it. The parent represents the overall issue; children represent component tasks or sub-issues assigned to different teams.

When to use child cases:

- A complex issue requires parallel work by multiple teams (e.g., a product defect involving Engineering, QA, and Documentation).

- Different components of the issue have different SLAs or owners.

- You need separate tracking of resolution for each sub-issue while maintaining a single customer-facing parent case.

How it works: the parent case can be configured to auto-close when all child cases are closed (via Flow). The customer-facing communication occurs on the parent; internal tracking occurs on children.

Limitation: Salesforce supports only one level of parent-child nesting (children cannot have their own child cases).

topics.question: How to associate multiple contacts with a single case using case contact relationships, and the limitations of the standard case contact field versus a custom relationship
topics.answer:
Standard Case Contact field: a single lookup to one Contact. By default, a case can only be linked to one contact at a time.

Multiple contacts: use the Case Contact Role or a custom junction object to link multiple contacts to a single case.

- Enable Case Contact Roles (if available in your org) to create multiple contact associations with role labels (e.g., "Primary Contact," "CC'd Contact").

- Alternatively, create a custom junction object (CaseContact__c) with lookups to Case and Contact for full flexibility.

Limitations of the standard field:

- Only one contact can be linked natively.

- Email notifications go only to the case's primary contact.

- Customer-facing portal visibility is limited to the primary contact's profile.

For multi-stakeholder cases (e.g., enterprise accounts with multiple contacts involved), a custom relationship is necessary.

topics.question: How to configure case close templates and required closure fields to ensure data completeness for reporting and quality analysis
topics.answer:
- Case Close Layout: Setup > Cases > Case Close Page Layouts. Configure a specific page layout for the case close action with required fields.

- Required closure fields: commonly required fields include: Resolution Summary, Root Cause, Close Reason, Time Spent, Knowledge Article (Was an article attached?).

- Validation Rules: add validation rules that fire only when Status = "Closed" to enforce that required fields are populated before closure is allowed.

- Close Case Quick Action: configure a Quick Action on the Case object for "Close Case" that presents the close layout as a modal — agents complete required fields without navigating away.

Data completeness at closure is critical for FCR reporting, root cause analysis, and Knowledge article creation.

topics.question: How the case merge feature works, its limitations, and when a consultant should recommend merging duplicate cases versus linking them
topics.answer:
Case Merge: Salesforce allows merging up to 3 duplicate cases. The user selects a master case; related records (emails, comments, attachments) from the non-master cases are merged into the master.

Limitations:

- Maximum 3 cases per merge operation.

- The merge is irreversible — the non-master cases are deleted.

- Merge is done manually (no automated duplicate detection for cases, unlike Contacts/Leads).

- Only available in Lightning Experience (some limitations in Classic).

Merge vs. Link:

- Merge: when cases are true duplicates (same customer, same issue, created by different channels). Eliminates redundancy.

- Link (Parent-Child): when cases are related but distinct issues that need separate tracking. Preserves both records.

Recommend merging when the customer contacted support through two channels for the exact same issue. Recommend linking when issues are related but require separate resolution tracking.

topics.question: The difference between public and private case comments, when each is visible to customers in a self-service portal, and how to control comment visibility
topics.answer:
- Public comments: visible to customers in an Experience Cloud self-service portal. Use for customer-facing updates, resolution steps, and responses the customer should see.

- Private comments: visible only to internal Salesforce users (agents, supervisors). Use for internal notes, escalation details, or information not suitable for customer visibility.

Control mechanism:

- On the Case Comment record, the "Published" checkbox controls whether the comment is public. When checked, the comment appears in the Experience Cloud portal for the case owner contact.

- Agents must consciously check "Published" to make a comment visible externally — the default can be configured.

Best practice: make the default for new comments "Private" (unchecked) to prevent accidental exposure of internal notes to customers.

agentforceservice.title: Given a set of requirements, explain how case deflection strategies are delivered in Experience Cloud sites, Agentforce, and Knowledge.

objectives.title: Given a set of requirements, explain how case deflection strategies are delivered in Experience Cloud sites, Agentforce, and Knowledge.

topics.question: How to configure a self-service Experience Cloud site so that customers who search for help see Knowledge articles before being offered a case creation form
topics.answer:
- Place the Knowledge Search component prominently on the site's Help Center or Support page.

- Position the Case Creation form/button below the fold or behind a "Contact Us" link — not on the landing page.

- Enable Article Suggestions: as the customer types into the search bar, surface matching articles in a dropdown before they submit.
